content:
maya: Quick heads-up — during the INT8/GPTQ bakeoff for redwood-7b-v2 we saw a narrow but reproducible QA accuracy drop (~-2.9%) on the conversational eval suite. Looks like a tiny subset of prompts trigger large activation spikes in the mid layers (48-56). Want a short triage thread before we push canary.

maya: Sample peek from a trace (layer 52):
```
layer=52 channel=14 max=189.2 mean=0.12 std=1.43 kurtosis=38.5 zscore=11.8
layer=53 channel=7  max=94.6  mean=0.02 std=0.88 kurtosis=22.1 zscore=8.7
```

quant-bot: anomaly-detector: flagged layers [48,49,50,52,54,55,56], 23 channels total with kurtosis>20 and max>50. mechanism=activation-spike-rule-3

sam: Thanks — this smells like per-channel heavy tails that the GPTQ per-block scales amplify. Instead of hard skipping a layer (which breaks kv layout + complicates runtime), let's run an activation perturbation scan to characterize sensitivity.

sam: Quick pseudo: 
```
for L in layers_to_check:
  for alpha in [0.95, 0.9, 0.85, 0.8]:
    apply_scale(layer=L, scale=alpha)
    run_small_eval()
    record(delta_accuracy, latency)
```

jun: +1 to the scan. Proposal: "soft attenuation" — per-channel multiplicative scales in the runtime that only target the high-kurtosis channels. Formula idea: s_c = clamp(1 - gamma * (kurtosis_c - K0)/Kstd, 0.65, 1.0). That keeps tensor shapes and KV cache unchanged and is cheap (elementwise mul).

jun: For a quick heuristic: pick channels where kurtosis>15 AND max>40, set s=0.8; otherwise leave s=1.0. We can make gamma tunable per-model.

kyle: I ran a 1k-sample probe with GPTQ-int8 locally. Results (convo-bench subset):
- baseline FP16: 100.0 (norm)
- GPTQ-int8 w/o mitigation: 97.1 (-2.9)
- GPTQ-int8 + layer-wise alpha=0.9 (L=52..54): 98.0 (-2.0)
- GPTQ-int8 + soft-channel-clamp(s=0.85 on flagged channels): 99.2 (-0.8) 
- AWQ-int8 baseline: 99.0 (-1.0)
Latency hit for soft-clamp: +1.5% p50, memory unchanged.

kyle: So soft attenuation recovers most of the quality loss with tiny latency/throughput cost. Seems promising.

maya: Which quant path caused the spike? GPTQ only? AWQ? FP8?

sam: From quick logs: GPTQ-int8 amplifies the high-weight scale variance in those blocks the most — GPTQ was worst. AWQ did better but still had a few regressions on the same prompt set. FP8 had no regressions on this subset.

quant-bot: comparison-summary: {"FP16":0.0, "GPTQ-INT8":-2.9, "AWQ-INT8":-1.0, "FP8":-0.1} (numbers = convo-bench relative %)

jun: Actionable plan:
1) implement soft-attenuation shim in runtime as a per-model config (per-layer + per-channel scales). default off.
2) add detection rule: kurtosis>20 AND max>50 => auto-suggest attenuation s=0.8 in Optimize.
3) run full eval overnight for redwood-7b-v2 with soft attenuation enabled; compare conv-bench + MMLU + codeeval.
4) canary rollout: 5% traffic on dedicated pool, monitor regression/error metrics + latency.

maya: I opened PR #1124 with a minimal runtime patch that applies per-channel scales when provided. Link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/p/1124 (WIP). @sam @kyle can you review?

sam: Will review this afternoon. Also recommending for the console: expose per-route flag to fallback to FP16 if regression >1.5% sustained for 1h. That can be a short-term safety net.

kyle: I'll add a small dashboard card: per-layer activation kurtosis histogram + top 10 channels list + applied scale. That helps SRE/SE see mitigations in real-time.

maya: Great. If everyone signs off, I'll start broad runs overnight and report back tomorrow AM. Thanks. :thumbsup:
